items.item_text: Demonstrated effective supervisory skills including experience in recruitment, performance appraisal, identification and communication of expectations, discipline, and training.
Demonstrated experience in managing patient services and nursing staff in a private medical practice or community clinic.
Reporting to the Regional Director, the incumbent will oversee the administrative and clinical support functions for the assigned Community Clinic.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to: overseeing patient experience, access, financial and budgetary oversight, staff human resources oversight, clinician on/off-boarding, care coordination and communication, space management, supply-chain management, environment of care, clinical outcomes, medication management, quality and safety reporting, revenue cycle management, policy development and deployment for assigned practice. Responsibilities also includes following and adhering to personnel policy and procedure, recruiting qualified personnel, partnering with Lead physician, clinic leads/supervisors, Medical Director, and Director of Operations to assure an overall effective operation. Core Competencies for this role includes strategic and critical thinking, operational execution and problem-solving, strong interpersonal and communication skills, data-driven and ethical decision-making. commitment to CI-CARE vales and high emotional intelligence and team leadership.
Skill in analyzing information and procedures to define objectives, identify patterns and recognize alternatives and their implications.
Working knowledge of University and Hospital policies and procedures to appropriately manage patient registration, cashiering, risk management, and personnel.
Skill in operating a personal computer and software programs, including MS Word, and Excel Spreadsheet.
Working knowledge of the CareConnect system.

Interpersonal skills to promote a cooperative and productive work environment and to establish and maintain cooperative, productive working relationships with faculty, residents, medical students and staff from various social, cultural, and economic backgrounds.
Accounting skills to plan, prepare and analyze revenue and expense budgets.
Writing skills to prepare accurate and concise reports and memorandums that clearly convey information utilizing appropriate vocabulary and grammar.
Working knowledge of computerized appointment scheduling and registration system, and the ability to effectively train staff in the use of the system.
Working knowledge of major medical insurance plans.
Ability to work occasional weekends or evenings as required.
